title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
hook: Finding the prompts that make a model misbehave is slow if humans do it by hand. So use another language model to generate those attacks automatically — at scale.
key_points: One language model generates test prompts designed to make a target model produce harmful outputs.
A classifier scores the target's responses to flag failures like toxicity or leaked private data.
Automation surfaces many more failure cases, far faster than manual red-teaming.
Discovered issues can then guide fixes and safer training of the target model.
content_html: Ethan Perez, Saffron Huang, and colleagues showed you can red-team a language model using another language model. One model is prompted to generate test cases — questions and prompts likely to provoke bad behavior — and a separate classifier checks whether the target's replies are harmful. By automating the search for failures, they surfaced offensive content, private-data leaks, and other problems at a scale and speed that manual testing can't match.
extra_html:
How it works

The setup pairs a "red" language model that produces candidate attack prompts with a detector that evaluates the target model's responses for undesirable behavior. The authors explore several ways to generate prompts, from straightforward sampling to reinforcement learning that pushes the red model toward prompts most likely to elicit failures. Running this loop over many prompts builds up a catalog of cases where the target slips, which is hard to assemble by hand.

Why it matters

You can't fix harms you haven't found, and human red-teaming is expensive and limited in coverage. Using models to probe models scales the search dramatically, exposing weaknesses before deployment. The failure cases are not just diagnostic — they can feed back into training and filtering to make the target safer. This automated approach became an important tool in the broader effort to test and align language models.

prereqs.title: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
prereqs.hook: Show the model a few examples right in the prompt and it picks up the task — no fine-tuning, no gradient updates. GPT-3 turned prompting into the new programming.

flashcards.prompt: How does this approach red-team a target language model?

flashcards.prompt: What is the main advantage of automating red-teaming with models?

choices.text: It surfaces far more failure cases, much faster than manual testing
It guarantees the target has zero vulnerabilities
It removes the need for any classifier

flashcards.explanation_html: Automation scales the search dramatically, exposing more weaknesses than expensive, limited human red-teaming.

flashcards.prompt: Beyond diagnosis, how are discovered failure cases useful?

They are only useful as a public leaderboard
They retrain the red model exclusively
